results.fact: Which trailhead/valley is used to reach Trapper Lake
results.correct_value: The approach is from the Cascade Pass Trailhead (Cascade River Road) over Cascade Pass to Pelton Basin, then off-trail down to Trapper Lake; the Stehekin-valley side is a harder, less-used alternative.
results.evidence: The reader's internal resolution picked the wrong side. A 2015 trip report describes going in and out from the Cascade Pass trailhead: maintained trail to Pelton Basin camp, then a boot path down toward Pelton Creek and a faint fisherman's trail to the lake (5.5 h in). A separate 2024 report from a party who tried from Stehekin/Old Cottonwood found that line sketchy and says the most-used route comes from Pelton Basin; the lake's reference page puts it off the upper Stehekin River Trail, which is the trail through Pelton Basin. The row's itinerary, beta, turnaround, timing breakdown, comms and climate already say Cascade Pass; the Harlequin trailhead is also geographically impossible at the stated 7.5 mi to the lake (roughly 16 mi straight-line). RESIDUAL NOT PATCHED (out of scope): waypoints[0] and approach_logistics still name and pin Harlequin Campground (lat 48.347744, lng -120.713821, elev 1184); they need a pin repair to the Cascade Pass Trailhead (~48.4755, -121.0750, ~3,660 ft) before the TRAILHEAD card agrees. Also patched: two 'Devore Creek' references (a Lake Chelan drainage nowhere near this peak) and ferry-dependent seasonal/fee/road/hospital text.

patches.find: There is no road access to the Trapper Mountain area — reach Stehekin first via the Lady of the Lake ferry (Lake Chelan Boat Company) or floatplane (Chelan Airways) from Chelan, WA. From Stehekin Landing, take the Stehekin Valley Road (or park shuttle) about 4.5 miles to Harlequin Campground. Figure a full day of travel each way from Harlequin; most parties treat this as a 2-3 day trip with a camp at or below Trapper Lake.
patches.replace: Start at the Cascade Pass Trailhead at the end of Cascade River Road and follow the maintained trail over Cascade Pass and down the Stehekin side to Pelton Basin. From the lowest tent sites at Pelton Basin, leave the trail on a faint boot path dropping toward Pelton Creek; below that the fisherman's path to Trapper Lake appears and vanishes, so expect route-finding through brush and alder before a flat, marshy walk along the inlet stream to the lake. Most parties treat this as a 2-3 day trip with a camp at Trapper Lake. The lake can also be reached by a steep off-trail climb from the upper Stehekin valley, but that line is harder to locate and first requires reaching Stehekin by boat or floatplane.

results.evidence: Regional Cascade Pass/Horseshoe Basin camp list. Pelton Basin Camp does serve this route (the approach leaves the trail at Pelton Basin and it is a usable first/last night). results.evidence: Itinerary day-1 schedule ('~5,000 ft basin') and climate.bySeason.summer ('Trapper Lake (~5,000 ft)') contradict waypoints[1], beta and approach_variants (4,170 ft, matching the lake's reference elevation). Not patched because the itinerary day gains (2,400/2,700/700 = 5,800 = gain_ft) are built on a ~5,000 ft camp; with the lake at 4,170 ft and the 5,392-ft pass crossed each way, car-to-car gain is closer to ~6,300 ft and every day's gain/loss would need re-deriving together.

results.fact: Whether the route tops out on Trapper Mountain's summit
results.evidence: Both published trip reports (2012 first ski descent, and a 2024 car-to-car in 11h45m) say only that the party 'topped out' the couloir; neither describes reaching or not reaching the 7,530-ft true summit or the ground between. The climbing_route caveat is accurate; high_point_ft/summit waypoint cannot be confirmed or refuted from available sources.

Same regional Horseshoe Basin/Cascade Pass list. Pelton Basin Camp is on this route's approach (via Cascade Pass) and serves it; Basin Creek/Cottonwood are on the Stehekin-side variant only; Sahale Glacier, Doubtful Lake and Buckner zone do not serve it. Trapper Lake (the stated base) is absent.

results.fact: Whether rappels are used on the descent

results.fact: What gates the start of the climbing season
results.correct_value: The season is gated by snow on the ridge/glacier, not a road; SR-20 to Colonial Creek is open year-round.
results.evidence: Internal: road, access.closures and approach_logistics all place this route on SR-20/Thunder Creek, west of the Ross Dam winter gate; Tricouni trip reports start from Colonial Creek (one in April), so no road gate governs the season. access.seasonal and climate.bySeason.spring repeated the same wrong-corridor claim and were patched too.
